P(A) = 0.4, P(B) = 0.5, P(A and B) = 0.2. Find P(A or B).
Two independent events with probabilities 0.5 and 0.2. P(both)?
A coin is tossed 3 times. P(at least one head)? (decimal)
Mutually exclusive events are the same as independent events.
why: Myth. Mutually exclusive events cannot happen together, so knowing one happened tells you the other didn't: they are dependent.
